entry_conditions: World-frame state input is required: qpos 0:9 (seven arm radians and two finger positions in metres), qvel 9:18, TCP pose 18:25, red pose 25:32, blue pose 32:39 (xyz metres and wxyz), drawer_position 39:40 in metres and drawer_velocity 40:41 in m/s. Supply the actual two causal observations where available. Demonstrated initial entry has d=0, drawer velocity=0, arm qpos=[0,-0.3,0,-2.1,0,1.8,0.7854], each finger=0.04 m, TCP approximately [-0.384,0,0.442] m, red z=0.063 m and blue z=0.020 m. The full training slice also supports mid-approach and transition entries on the observed manipulation manifold; the overlap begins near d=0.1863 m with positive drawer velocity approximately 0.1071 m/s and fingers approximately 0.0071 m each. Cabinet pose and world -X prismatic axis are assumed fixed, not inferred from images.
exit_conditions: The drawer-opening milestone d>0.26 m precedes several useful transition states. At d approximately 0.300 m, the demonstrated tool first remains near the handle with narrow fingers, then opens to about 0.04 m per finger and retreats upward. After red approach it closes around red to approximately 0.0182 m per finger. The supplied post-final-action boundary measurements have red center z approximately 0.142-0.143 m and TCP z approximately 0.143-0.144 m, with TCP about 0.009 m on red's -X side, near-zero Y separation, and upward lift already underway. Source pre-action states at demo1000:474 and demo1001:475 have red z approximately 0.133 m, just before those boundary states. Commands are still g=-1 there. Preserve that grasp and continue lifting at late transfer. These are supported examples, not millimetre acceptance tolerances or proof of contact.
overlap_role: open_access learns every assigned action from 0 through stop-1; its overlap with evacuate_red is [195,stop), where stop is 474, 475 or 476 according to trajectory. This is 279-281 actions, not just a boundary pose. It learns continuation of loaded pulling, completion of opening, handle release, upward retreat to TCP z about 0.369 m, rotation and approach above red, descent with open fingers, closing and initial red lift. Moving-drawer TCP offsets encode the handle vicinity without assuming a measured handle pose. Red-minus-drawer and red-minus-TCP features remain available during the entire change of interaction, instead of switching off after opening.
successor_readiness: Pass qpos/qvel, both causal TCP/red/blue poses, drawer position and velocity to evacuate_red. At an early overlap handoff, d may still be below 0.26 m, TCP is near the handle at z approximately 0.128 m, fingers are approximately 0.0071 m each and d is rising: the successor must finish pulling, release and retreat before approaching red. At intermediate handoff, d approximately 0.300 m plus wide fingers, elevated TCP and stationary red distinguish retreat or approach from a loaded pull. At a late handoff, the near-fixed TCP-minus-red offset, approximately 0.0182 m fingers and positive consecutive red/TCP height changes are evidence consistent with a held red block; the successor should maintain closing and continue lift before translation. An open drawer alone is insufficient to infer which of these motions is next.
failure_signatures: Alarm observations include d not rising while TCP moves -X in the apparent pulling configuration, unexpected red motion relative to the drawer before pickup, d falling below 0.26 m after opening, closing fingers without subsequent red/TCP co-lift, or beginning red approach while the tool appears still attached to the handle. Red x+d is only approximately conserved because the demonstrations include initial slip; do not reject small deviations as failure. Contact and attachment here are inferred from geometry, aperture and motion, not measured forces. These alarms identify unsupported or unsuccessful behavior; the demonstrations do not establish a recovery policy.
continuation_guidance: Recompute causal relational features and execute short learned DDPM prefixes with observation feedback. Continue this policy when still pulling, releasing, retreating, approaching or beginning the supported red lift unless the inference agent elects a compatible overlap transfer. Do not reset to the initial approach merely because invocation starts mid-transition, and do not open the gripper merely because d>0.26 m. Transfer to red evacuation by the demonstrated initial-lift exit instead of expecting this model to transport red to the pad. There is no model-side scripted phase schedule, grasp gate or termination controller. Handoff guidance never adds a sustained hold, speed, release or TCP-clearance requirement to the task completion contract.
limitations: Observed support comes from twelve successful demonstrations with near-identical opening motion and modest placement variation. Arbitrary open-drawer starts, blocked mechanisms, changed cabinet pose, poor grasps and sensor noise are untested. A two-frame causal policy has no clock to reproduce indistinguishable stationary dwell durations. Quaternion-sign-invariant orientation features do not imply global SE(3) invariance or joint-action equivariance. Drawer-relative geometry is a representation bias, not collision avoidance, IK, force control, a grasp detector or a guarantee of d staying open. This slice ends during red lift; task success still requires drawer open, red on its pad and blue inside the drawer at the same observation under the supplied evaluator.
